You are implementing exactly ONE change request in a checkout of the Django web framework (version 3.2 development, Python 3.9).

Your current working directory is an ISOLATED git worktree of the repository. It is a full, working Django source tree. Nobody else is editing it. Work only inside it.

## The change request

Read the file `requirements/random-string-alphabet-constant.yaml` in your working directory. It contains `title`, `category` and `requirement` fields. The text is a paraphrase / rewrite of the commit message of a REAL upstream Django commit that was made on top of this exact tree state. Your job is to reproduce that upstream change as faithfully and completely as you can infer it.

## How to work

1. Read the requirement file completely. The title usually contains the upstream ticket ("Fixed #12345 -- ...") and is a strong hint about the affected component.
2. Locate the relevant code. Use `grep -rn`, `Grep`, `Glob` over `django/`, `tests/`, and `docs/`. Read enough surrounding code to understand the existing design and conventions.
3. Implement the change:
   - Change the library source under `django/` when the requirement describes a behaviour/bug/feature change.
   - Update or add tests under `tests/` when the requirement describes testable behaviour, mentions a regression test, or is itself a test-only change. Put tests in the existing test module/class that covers that area; follow its style exactly.
   - Update documentation under `docs/` when the requirement is about docs, deprecations, new public API, or release notes for a new feature/deprecation. Do not invent release notes for plain bug fixes.
   - If the requirement is a pure cleanup/typo/refactor, make exactly that cleanup and nothing more.
4. Match the surrounding code style: same naming, same comment density, same import ordering (isort-compatible), 4-space indent, max line length 119, no trailing whitespace. Django source uses single quotes predominantly.
5. Be complete but MINIMAL and SURGICAL. Do not reformat unrelated code, do not "improve" nearby code, do not bump version numbers, do not touch `AUTHORS`.
6. NEVER modify any of these paths: `requirements/`, `requirement_patches/`, `agent_plans/`, `agent_tests/`, `.claude/`, `Django.egg-info/`. Do not create files at the repository root.
7. Verify. Run the focused tests you touched (and the closest existing suite) like this:
   `cd tests && python3 runtests.py --parallel=1 <label> 2>&1 | tail -30`
   where `<label>` is e.g. `admin_views.test_history_view` or `queries`. Databases available: sqlite (default) only. If a test needs postgres/oracle/mysql it will be skipped — that is fine, but make sure it at least imports and collects. Also byte-compile files you edited: `python3 -m py_compile <files>`.
8. Iterate until the focused tests pass (or are legitimately skipped for lack of a backend).

## Deliverable (MANDATORY)

From the ROOT of your worktree, run exactly:

    git add -A && git diff --cached --binary > /tmp/wfp/random-string-alphabet-constant.patch && wc -c /tmp/wfp/random-string-alphabet-constant.patch

The patch MUST be non-empty and MUST contain only your intended change. Before writing it, run `git status --short` and `git diff --cached --stat` and confirm nothing unrelated (stray scratch files, `.pyc`, editor backups, `PROBE.txt`-style files) is included; delete any such file first. Never produce an empty patch: if you are unsure of the exact upstream change, still make the best-reasoned faithful change you can.

Also write a short report file `/tmp/wfp/random-string-alphabet-constant.json` containing a JSON object with keys `slug`, `status`, `files` (array of repo-relative paths you changed), `tests` (the runtests.py labels you ran and their result), and `reasoning` (2-6 sentences on what you changed and why).

## Return value

Return ONLY the structured object: slug, status ('done' if you are confident the change is complete and verified, 'partial' if implemented but unverified/uncertain, 'failed' if you could not produce a patch), and a note of at most 400 characters summarising the change (files + one-line description). Keep the note terse.

---
You are running in an isolated git worktree at /workspace/.claude/worktrees/wf_30c177c0-67f-5 (a separate working copy of the repo). Changes you make here do NOT affect the main working directory (/workspace) or other agents. Work normally — the worktree will be cleaned up automatically if you made no changes, or preserved for review if you did.

Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

title: 'Refs #31358 -- Added constant for get_random_string()''s default alphabet.'
category: feature
requirement: 'Code that needs Django''s default random-string alphabet should be able to reference a named constant instead of depending on a duplicated literal. Expose a constant for `get_random_string()`''s default alphabet so callers and internal code can share the same contract while leaving the actual default-character behavior unchanged. This is a small developer-facing API cleanup aimed at consistency, not a behavior change.

  '

    21	    Return the HMAC of 'value', using a key generated from key_salt and a
    22	    secret (which defaults to settings.SECRET_KEY). Default algorithm is SHA1,
    23	    but any algorithm name supported by hashlib.new() can be passed.
    24	
    25	    A different key_salt should be passed in for every application of HMAC.
    26	    """

    41	    key = hasher(key_salt + secret).digest()
